title: Computers, Software and AI: Understanding the Differences
introduction: This lesson explains what a computer is, what software does, how traditional programs work, and how AI systems are different. Knowing these basics helps you see how everyday technology works.

sections.heading: What Is a Computer?
paragraphs: A computer is a physical machine made of electronic parts. It can store, retrieve, and process information quickly.
The main hardware parts are the CPU (brain), memory (short‑term storage), and storage devices like hard drives or SSDs (long‑term storage).

example.title: Home Desktop Example
example.content: A typical home desktop has a CPU, RAM, a hard drive, a monitor, keyboard, and mouse. All these parts work together to run programs.

sections.heading: Understanding Software
sections.subheading: Instructions that tell the computer what to do
paragraphs: Software is a set of instructions that tells the hardware how to perform tasks. It can be an app, a game, or a system program.
Software does not have a physical form; it exists as code stored on the computer’s storage and runs when needed.

example.title: Word Processor
example.content: Microsoft Word is software that lets you type, edit, and format documents. The hardware runs the Word program to display text on the screen.

sections.heading: Traditional Programs and Automation
sections.subheading: Rule‑based instructions that follow a set path
paragraphs: Traditional programs follow explicit steps written by a programmer. They execute the same way every time given the same input.
Automation uses these rule‑based programs to perform repetitive tasks without human help.

example.title: Thermostat Automation
example.content: A programmable thermostat turns heating on when the room temperature falls below 20°C and turns it off when it rises above 22°C. The rules are fixed and do not change.

sections.heading: How AI Systems Differ
sections.subheading: Learning from data instead of fixed rules
paragraphs: AI systems use data to learn patterns and make decisions. They are not limited to a single set of hard‑coded rules.
When new data is added, an AI model can improve its performance, unlike traditional programs that stay the same unless rewritten.

example.title: Voice Assistant
example.content: A voice assistant like Siri learns from many voice recordings. Over time it gets better at understanding different accents and new words.

practice.title: Classify the Example
practice.instruction: Look at each item below and decide if it is hardware, traditional software, or an AI system. Write your answer for each: (1) A laptop computer, (2) A calculator app, (3) A spam‑filter that improves over time.

keyTakeaways: A computer is the physical hardware that runs programs.
Software is a set of instructions that tell hardware what to do.
AI systems learn from data and can change their behavior, unlike fixed rule‑based programs.

mcqs.question: What is the primary function of the CPU in a computer?
options: It stores long‑term data
It displays graphics on the monitor
It processes instructions as the computer's brain
It provides power to the system
mcqs.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) executes instructions and performs calculations, acting as the brain of the computer.

mcqs.question: How does a traditional program behave when given the same input multiple times?
options: It produces the same output each time
It changes its output each time
It learns from the input and improves
It randomly decides what to do
mcqs.explanation: Traditional programs follow fixed, rule‑based instructions, so identical inputs always lead to identical outputs.

mcqs.question: Which of the following examples best illustrates an AI system?
options: A programmable thermostat that turns heating on or off
A voice assistant that learns from many recordings
A hard‑drive that stores files
A word processor used to edit documents
mcqs.explanation: A voice assistant learns from data (voice recordings) and improves over time, which is characteristic of AI systems.

mcqs.question: What is the main difference between AI systems and traditional software?
options: AI systems can be rewritten easily
AI systems use fixed rule sets
AI systems improve performance when new data is added
AI systems require no hardware
mcqs.explanation: AI models are trained on data; adding new data lets them learn new patterns and become better, unlike fixed rule‑based programs.

mcqs.question: In the practice classification, which item is hardware?
options: Calculator app
Spam‑filter that improves over time
Voice assistant
Laptop computer
mcqs.explanation: A laptop computer is a physical machine made of electronic parts, which classifies it as hardware.
